primitives.verbatim_quote: dividing (scc Table 9) the male and female parents respectively into three nearly equal groups, of tall, medium, and short.
primitives.assumptions: (1) Parents are categorized into three ordered groups based on measured statures; (2) Equal group sizes are approximated due to measurement discreteness; (3) Group assignments are nominal rather than precise thresholds.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Discrete categorization fails when sample size approaches zero or measurement error dominates true variance.

primitives.name: Marriage Contrast-Likelihood Ratio
primitives.verbatim_quote: In other words, there were 32 cases of contrast in marriage, to 27 cases of likeness.
primitives.assumptions: (1) Marriage choices are modeled as binary outcomes (contrast vs. likeness); (2) The ratio 32:27 represents empirical frequencies under the observed data.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Ratio collapses to indeterminacy when either count approaches zero, indicating sparse sampling failure.

primitives.name: Stature-Independent Marriage Assumption
primitives.verbatim_quote: I am therefore content to ignore it, and to regard the Statures of married folk just as if their choice in marriage had been wholly independent of stature.
primitives.assumptions: (1) Marriage selection is statistically independent of parental statures; (2) This simplifies joint distribution factorization into marginals.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Independence assumption breaks down when heritable traits exhibit assortative mating patterns, inducing covariance structure.

layer2.telemetry: Mutual information between parental statures under empirical versus independent distributions.

However, this simplification introduces bias when assortative mating exists, leading to misestimation of heritability and genetic correlation.
